PUCIOCOUNTS COUGHS

Pucio and Artur listen to the night

1

One day at the clinic

Kasia fits a recorder on a patient.

Today, the patient hardly coughs.

The Professor waits with his clipboard.

Pucio looks at the clock.

Trials judge new cough drugs by objective coughs per hour, usually from a 24-hour recording at each of a few clinic visits.

3

Which day is real?

Monday’s chart is full of coughs.

Tuesday’s chart is nearly empty.

The Professor only has Tuesday.

Pucio holds up a calendar. “Which day is the real one?”

Daily cough counts vary by about 38%. In one study, a single day missed the longer-term pattern for two thirds of participants.

4 · S5

The expensive box

The Professor asks for more nights.

Artur unpacks the monitor.

The Professor looks in his wallet.

Kasia hands Pucio a form. “Cough a little or a lot?”

A gold-standard monitor costs about €11,000 plus 1.5 h of analysis per recording. Researchers in the Danish studies we reviewed used questionnaires or registries.

Cough research needs a way to count more nights at lower cost.

6

Nothing to wear

Artur draws a vest with 37 sensors.

Kasia says, “No patient will sleep in that.”

Pucio walks over to the bed.

He puts a little box on the nightstand.

The bedside smart-home assistant automatically counts coughs every night. There’s nothing to wear, and it stores no audio.

7

Every night, at home

The box counts coughs while the patient sleeps.

The air dries. The humidifier switches on.

Kasia and the Professor see each night’s count.

Pucio hides Artur’s confetti. “First, the trial.”

Researchers get objective cough counts across multiple nights at home. Patients get a device that helps manage their bedroom climate.

9

Who it’s for

User
PhD student or postdoc who runs study recordings
Buyer
Principal investigator who holds the grant budget
First interview targets
Rigshospitalet, Herlev-Gentofte, Aarhus and SDU (S13)

Study scope

  • Research use only. No diagnosis or sales to clinics or patients.
  • VitaloJAK stays in place for large pharma trials.
  • Chronic-cough studies are the initial focus. COPD and asthma care are outside scope.
  • Investigational device for studies via the ethics committee route (S12).

We start with academic chronic-cough studies and test whether cost limits access to objective counts.
